extracted.intended_audience: advanced students and scholars of mechanics and history/philosophy of physics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and methodological criteria for assessing Newton's definitions, laws, and experiments in classical mechanics; emphasizes empirical testability, operational definitions, and correct interpretation of experiments (e.g., bucket, globes, rotating vessel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrifugal forces as criterion for absolute motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects by which absolute and relative motions are distinguished from one another, are centrifugal forces, or those forces in circular motion which produce a tendency of recession from the axis. For in a circular motion which is purely relative no such forces exist; but in a true and absolute circular motion they do exist, and are greater or less according to the quantity of the [absolute] motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Newton's bucket experiment: water surface becomes concave as vessel's motion is communicated to the water; initially relative motion produces no recession, but later the rising at the sides indicates real circular motion. Also illustrated by two globes connected by a cord: cord tension reveals tendency to recede and hence allows computation of quantity and direction of circular motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experiments to detect true motion (bucket/globes/tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical effects (e.g., water surface shape, cord tension between rotating globes) are the markers by which true motions and their quantities/directions can be discovered even in an immense vacuum where nothing sensible with which the globes could be compared exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure centrifugal tendencies (e.g., tension, rise at sides) and changes under applied forces to deduce quantity and direction of circular motion; determine which faces 'follow' to infer motion direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of empirical testability; avoid predicating absolute space
rubrics_metrics.description: No one is competent to predicate things about absolute space and absolute motion; they are pure things of thought, pure mental constructs, that cannot be produced in experience. All our principles of mechanics are experimental knowledge concerning the relative positions and motions of bodies. No one is warranted in extending these principles beyond the boundaries of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories and principles must be tied to experimentally accessible relations of bodies; avoid asserting untestable metaphysical constructs as physical facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate law of inertia relative to other masses (mean acceleration = 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of referring a moving body to 'space', view its relation to the bodies of the universe: the mean acceleration of a mass mu with respect to the masses m, m', m'' at distances r, r', r'' is = 0 (or equivalent integral expression). This expression is equivalent to the ordinary law of inertia when a sufficient number of distant masses is taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application requires a sufficient number of sufficiently distant and large masses; the expression d*(2mr/2 m)/dt* = 0 (or analogous integral over space) formalizes inertia without invoking absolute space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/dynamical definitions (mass from dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition I (mass as measure by density and volume) is a pseudo-definition; the true definition of mass can be deduced only from the dynamical relations of bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer definitions tied to observable dynamical quantities (e.g., proposed: mass-ratio of two bodies equals the negative inverse ratio of their mutually induced accelerations) rather than purely geometric or volumetric descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tautology in laws; laws must add substantive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws I and II (inertia and proportionality of change of motion to impressed force) are contained in the preceding definitions of force and acceleration; thus stating them again can be tautological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that laws are not mere restatements of definitional choices but supply experimentally nontrivial content or assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third law depends on empirically established mass concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The third law (reaction equal and opposite to action) is unintelligible without the correct idea of mass, which must itself be obtained from dynamical experience; thus the law's status depends on prior empirical establishment of mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish mass operationally from experiments before invoking reciprocal-action principles; avoid circular reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly state empirical assumption of independence (superposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The accelerations which any number of bodies A, B, C induce in a body K are independent of each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This empirical proposition is the basis for the parallelogram (vector) composition of forces; it should be acknowledged as an experimental fact rather than a self-evident axiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance of mass-ratios across physical states
rubrics_metrics.description: The mass-ratios of bodies are independent of the character of the physical states (of the bodies) that condition the mutual accelerations produced, be those states electrical, magnetic, or what not; and they remain, moreover, the same, whether they are mediately or immediately arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat mass as an intrinsic dynamical quantity unaffected by the particular interaction mechanism; verify experimentally across different interaction types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of moving force as mass times acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: Moving force is the product of the mass-value of a body into the acceleration induced in that body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the operational definition linking 'force' to measurable mass and acceleration (proposed substitution e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of mechanics require continual experimental control
rubrics_metrics.description: The apparently simplest mechanical principles are of a very complicated nature and are founded on incomplete experiences, nay on experiences that never can be fully completed; they can by no means themselves be regarded as mathematically established truths but only as principles that not only admit of constant control by experience but actually require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat fundamental principles as provisional and subject to refinement as new experimental or astronomical knowledge becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret experiments to accord with known facts, not fictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our business is to bring experiments into accord with the other facts known to us, and not with the arbitrary fictions of our imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple interpretations exist (e.g., Ptolemaic vs Copernican), prefer the one that best accords with experience and that is simpler and more practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider hypothetical space-filling medium only if testable and useful
rubrics_metrics.description: One might picture some medium filling all space that determines motion instead of Newton's absolute space; although nothing practical is accomplished with this conception at present, from the point of view of science it would be more valuable than the forlorn idea of absolute space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesize such media cautiously; pursue further hydrodynamical/kinetic study and only adopt if it yields testable predictions superior to alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require sufficient reference bodies to determine motion/coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion of a body K can only be estimated by reference to other bodies A, B, C ... ; since we always have at our disposal a sufficient number of bodies that are relatively fixed or slowly changing their positions, we are in such reference restricted to no one definite body and can alternately leave out one or another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coordinate systems and statements of motion specify the reference ensemble and note limitations when relatively fixed bodies are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overextend principles beyond empirically given cases
rubrics_metrics.description: It is impossible to say whether the new expression would still represent the true condition of things if the stars were to perform rapid movements among one another; the general experience cannot be constructed from the particular case given us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting universal validity of principles in regimes not yet observed; await empirical data before generalizing.
